water.name: Coast
water.rule: Sea within 200 m of the shore, or shallower than 200 m.

relief.name: Flat
relief.rule: Mean elevation under 500 m and little internal variation.

relief.name: Hills
relief.rule: Mean elevation 500-1,500 m, or a spread over 260 m.

relief.name: Mountains
relief.rule: Mean elevation over 1,500 m, or a spread over 900 m.

relief.name: High peaks
relief.rule: Mean elevation over 3,400 m, or a peak above 4,600 m.

cover.name: None
cover.rule: No land sample (water or outside India).

cover.name: Deciduous forest
cover.rule: Moist and dry deciduous forest: the sal and teak belts of central India and the Eastern Ghats.

cover.name: Evergreen forest
cover.rule: Evergreen and semi-evergreen forest: the Western Ghats, the Northeast and the Andamans.

cover.name: Mixed forest
cover.rule: Hill forest mixing conifer and broadleaf, mainly the Himalaya.

cover.name: Scrub & thorn
cover.rule: Thorn scrub and dry savanna where crops and forest are both thin.

cover.name: Pasture
cover.rule: Grazed and fallow land around the fields.

cover.name: Cropland
cover.rule: Net sown area: the rice, wheat, cotton and pulse belts.

cover.name: Wetland
cover.rule: Marsh, mangrove, delta and flooded paddy.

cover.name: Barren
cover.rule: Rock, sand and high-altitude waste, including the Thar and the trans-Himalaya.

cover.name: Snow & ice
cover.rule: Permanent snow and glacier above the snow line.

tables.notes: Cover is modelled from district land-use statistics (forest cover, net sown area, urban share) with elevation, relief and river proximity, then textured. It is not a pixel land-cover classification.
